doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Making a living in New York
summary: Early hard times in New York and taking any kind of work.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So from a financial standpoint, you had a family and so forth, was it tough to make a living in New York or were there a series of years that it was tougher than others?

It was very tough when I first arrived and got my 802 card. I didn’t know anybody. I came off the road from playing with name bands. Who cares in New York? And little by little I got to know some people and actually worked my way, opened a few doors. And here again, Dick Hyman was most instrumental in that process for me.
Did you ever need to work a non-music job?
No I never did. I worked a lot of jobs that weren’t music in the strict sense.
But not disassociated from the so-called business, no.
Well I would imagine being in your position that you took a lot of different kinds of work.
Bar mitzvahs and all kinds of stuff.
